extracted.intended_audience: U.S. policymakers, federal agencies (War/Navy/Commerce), Congress, university and research leaders, and the scientific community
extracted.subtask_description: Policy guidance for federal support, organization, and dissemination of scientific research in the postwar United States, covering national security, basic research, institutional roles, personnel, funding levels, and publication/declassification. Aimed at shaping programs and legislation to renew and expand scientific capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific research essential to national security
rubrics_metrics.description: In this war it has become clear beyond all doubt that scientific research is absolutely essential to national security; scientific techniques (e.g., radar) have been decisive in military outcomes and will be crucial in future preparedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and call upon research scientists in peacetime to continue substantial contributions to national security; recognize the competitive time element in developing weapons/tactics and the necessity of civilian participation alongside the armed services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government responsibility for military research
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be more—and more adequate—military research during peacetime; only the Government can undertake much military research since it must be carried on in secret, often has no commercial value, and is expensive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government obligation to support research on military problems is inescapable; create permanent civilian activity to supplement service R&D and a permanent independent, civilian-controlled organization with close liaison to Army and Navy, funds directly from Congress, and clear power to initiate military research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic research as foundation for jobs and economic growth
rubrics_metrics.description: A stream of new scientific knowledge is required to create new and better products, reduce costs, and thus promote full employment and higher standards of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in basic research and training of scientists and engineers because industrial and public enterprise depend on new knowledge and trained personnel to innovate and compete internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance and nature of basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic research is performed without thought of practical ends, produces general knowledge, and provides the scientific capital from which practical applications are eventually drawn; its results are unpredictable and come via many varied paths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize basic research as the pacemaker of technological progress; avoid neglecting it since dependence on external basic discoveries will slow industrial progress and weaken competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universities and institutes as centers of basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly and privately supported colleges, universities, and endowed research institutes must furnish new scientific knowledge and trained research workers; they are uniquely qualified by tradition and characteristics to carry on basic research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support these institutions so they remain strong and healthy, attract top scientists as teachers/investigators, offer research opportunities and sufficient compensation to compete with industry and government; preserve their intellectual freedom and the environment that allows work challenging current beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government research should focus on public-interest applied fields and be strengthened
rubrics_metrics.description: Most government laboratory research is applied; government is dependent on colleges/universities for basic frontiers but government research must be expanded in areas of public importance not adequately carried by private organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthen/expand government research where appropriate; improve procedures for recruiting, classifying, and compensating scientific personnel so government can compete for first-class talent; avoid organizational fragmentation by pursuing some coordination of policies and budgets among scientific agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a Science Advisory Board for coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a real need for some measure of coordination of common scientific activities of government agencies, both as to policies and budgets, and at present no such means exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a permanent Science Advisory Board composed of disinterested scientists (no connections with government agencies) to consult with scientific bureaus and advise executive and legislative branches on policies and budgets of government scientific research agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government role in strengthening industrial research
rubrics_metrics.description: The simplest and most effective way the Government can strengthen industrial research is by supporting basic research and developing scientific talent; small enterprises may not equally receive benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study and consider establishing 'research clinics' to help small enterprises make better use of research; protect and develop scientific talent that industry can later apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax policy must clarify treatment of R&D expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: Uncertainties as to the Internal Revenue Service treatment of R&D expense deductions deter research expenditure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend the Internal Revenue Code to remove present uncertainties regarding the deductibility of research and development expenditures as current charges against net income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent system should be maintained and abuses corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent laws stimulate invention and industry creation but uncertainties and abuses have impaired small industries' ability to translate ideas into valuable products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct patent abuses and clarify operation; withhold specific action pending a detailed report (Secretary of Commerce-led) and the National Patent Planning Commission findings, but ensure the patent system continues to serve its constitutional purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote international exchange of scientific information
rubrics_metrics.description: Increasing specialization makes it important that scientists keep abreast of developments abroad; scientific exchange is a facet of international accord.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government should aid international congresses, accredit and receive scientists officially, facilitate rapid flow of technical information (including translation services), and consider international fellowships; private foundations partly fulfill these roles but government should take an active role to complete the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special need for federal support of basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: Because wartime Europe can no longer be relied upon as a source of fundamental knowledge and because basic research is essentially noncommercial, new impetus for domestic research must come from the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide prompt federal expenditures to strengthen college/university/basic-research capacity; strive to preserve private support while supplementing it with public funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide adequate funding scale (cost estimate)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adequate federal program supporting basic research in colleges, universities, research institutes and financing important applied research in the public interest will cost about $10 million at the outset and may rise to about $50 million annually when fully underway (in perhaps 5 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and plan federal commitments recognizing these magnitude estimates as the start-up and steady-state funding targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational policy must renew scientific talent without crowding out other fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of new scientific knowledge rests on the small body of trained scientists; educational policy determines scientific progress. Programs expanding science must not draw disproportionately from humanities and social sciences to the nation's detriment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design programs that preserve balance among fields of national welfare; avoid creating an elite siphoning off all high ability into science—use broad opportunity and successive selection ('skimmings') at higher levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection strategy: broad base with successive refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: A plan cannot reliably select only future scientific leaders; therefore a relatively large base of high ability should be selected for development with successive selection at higher levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer widespread opportunity so ability, not circumstance, determines progress; remove ceilings to intellectual ambition while using successive opportunity to identify and elevate top performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove economic and access barriers to higher education in science
rubrics_metrics.description: Higher education largely favors those with means; many talented individuals lack means and are lost to science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ability, not family fortune, determines access to higher education; improve high school instruction, provide local help to finish high school, increase college access for promising students, and use scholarships/fellowships to reduce financial barriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salvage scientific talent in uniform
rubrics_metrics.description: The war has created an accumulating deficit of trained scientific personnel; many potential scientists are serving in the armed forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Armed Services should comb records for those with evidence of scientific talent and arrange, consistent with discharge plans, to send those who can benefit to institutions (domestic or overseas) to continue scientific education and ensure access to the latest developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarships, fellowships, and a National Science Reserve
rubrics_metrics.description: To encourage and enable more young people to take up science and reduce the deficit, provision should be made for undergraduate scholarships, graduate fellowships, and fellowships for advanced training and fundamental research; recipients enrolled in a National Science Reserve liable for call in national emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work out details with States and institutions without impairing institutional freedom; follow proposed scales (Moe Committee plan: 24,000 undergraduate scholarships and 900 graduate fellowships; cost ~ $30,000,000 annually; yearly flow: 6,000 undergraduate, 300 graduate awards) as a model for scale and allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lift wartime security restrictions promptly to disseminate knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Much wartime scientific information is confined by classifications; except where military security dictates otherwise, such knowledge should be spread upon the record for public benefit and national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release classified material as soon as it is safe (enemy cannot exploit); release information needed by industry and education without disclosing military embodiments; broad dissemination aids further advances and national security more than prolonged restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate declassification and release among agencies and allies
rubrics_metrics.description: Research was conducted under many auspices and some information is jointly held with allies; uncoordinated release could be unfair or create international friction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate release plans across Army, Navy, OSRD, NACA, other departments, educational institutions, industrial organizations, and with allies to prevent unfairness, morale problems, or international friction from sporadic uncontrolled release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a Board to control declassification and release
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should recommend release of information from military classification; it should be an Army, Navy, civilian body, well grounded in science and technology, competent to advise Secretaries and have sufficient recognition for prompt decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a Board made up equally of scientists and military men to pass upon declassification and control the release for publication of scientific information now classified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage preparation and publication of wartime scientific results
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond declassification, material should be prepared and published in forms and at prices which facilitate dissemination and use; OSRD has arranged for manuscript preparation while staffs are assembled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide for preparation and publication as soon as possible to facilitate broad dissemination; support publication efforts and ensure affordability and accessibility.
